body:
## Summary
CI's lanes are a hand-maintained list of steps, and the list has already fallen behind the repo: three Python suites (125 tests, among them the voice sidecar's JSON-lines protocol the daemon speaks) are gates in every local brief but never run on a pull request, while the README tells readers CI runs everything. Derive the lane set from the workspace's own manifests and make a missing, stale or unparseable lane a red build.

## Description
Add `scripts/ci-lanes.mjs` (Node, no dependencies). It derives the expected lanes - every workspace package (pnpm-workspace.yaml globs) x its gate scripts {check, typecheck, test, lint, build}, plus every `tools/*` Python suite (a `tests/` package -> `unittest discover`; top-level `test_*.py` -> those modules) - then reads ci.yml's `run:` lines and reports uncovered lanes, stale lanes (naming a package that does not exist) and run lines it cannot parse. `--check` exits non-zero on any of the three and always prints its checked denominator. Wire it as the first web step and add a `python` job (ubuntu, Python 3.12, `pip install numpy pillow`) running the three suites. Before the voice lane may block, make tools/voice/tests/test_pool.py:89 deterministic: assert `peak <= 2` for the bound the test is named after, and prove the overlap with fake sentences long enough (or gated) that both have started before either ends. A verdict that varies on an unchanged commit cannot gate.

Techniques: foreign-config-replay (pipeline-authoring - 'a check ran locally and was never scheduled in the pipeline'), blocking-by-input-determinism (quality-gates - 'a second language in the build that the test lanes never execute'; 'a gate whose verdict varies on an unchanged commit'), unparseable-form-is-a-finding and checked-vs-skipped-denominators for the planner's own honesty. Gate: architecture (CI topology). Coupled file outside the context: tools/voice/tests/test_pool.py (the lane cannot land red).

## Flow
- planner reads pnpm-workspace.yaml + each package.json scripts + tools/* layout -> expected lanes
- planner reads ci.yml run lines -> scheduled lanes (+ unparseable list)
- diff -> uncovered / stale / unparseable -> exit code + denominator line
- CI web job runs the planner first; new python job runs the three suites
- README Development section names the Python lane and the planner

## Expected impact
The voice sidecar protocol, the rig's layer spec and the avatar depth prep become merge-blocking for the first time; adding a gate script to any package (e.g. a future stage `lint`) without scheduling it turns CI red instead of drifting silently; README's 'all of them' becomes true and stays mechanically true.

## Evaluation
Claim: CI coverage of declared gates becomes derived and enforced.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no planner exists; Python lanes absent from ci.yml; test_pool intermittently red)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (node:test fixtures for the planner; the 20x loop for test_pool)
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: grep -n python .github/workflows/ci.yml -> no match; jobs are `rust:` (line 41) and `web:` (line 63). Local 2026-10-21: tools/voice `Ran 76 tests ... FAILED (failures=1, skipped=1)`: `FAIL: test_the_pool_never_runs_more_than_its_workers ... test_pool.py, line 89 ... AssertionError: 1 != 2`; three reruns of tests.test_pool: OK / FAILED (failures=1) / OK. Director baseline log for this run shows the same failure (voice-py=1). tools/rig `Ran 28 tests ... OK`; tools/avatar `Ran 21 tests ... OK`. README.md:38-39 'CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs all of them on each push to `main` and on every pull request'.

critic.reason: Valuable and grounded; one acceptance figure is inconsistent with the card's own derivation rule.

revision: In case 6 replace 'with N >= 22' with the exact count the planner's stated rule derives (17 web package-script lanes + the Python suites, stating whether rust lanes are counted), so the denominator is a checkable number rather than an unreachable bound.

title: The broadcast stage is the one package no lint gate reads: bring it under
acceptance: `pnpm -C apps/stage lint` on the built tree -> exit 0 with --max-warnings 0 (today no lint script exists; a read-only probe with the root rules finds 81 findings across 15 files)
seed `const x = y as unknown as Z` in apps/stage/src/source.ts -> lint exits 1 with the 'No `as unknown as`' message

probe (root config + a stage block, read-only, 2026-10-21): 81 findings - 46 react-hooks/refs (42 of all findings in App.tsx), 20 no-restricted-syntax, 6 no-restricted-properties, 9 other; console by contrast has zero `as unknown as` (grep -rln 'as unknown as' apps/console/src -> no output)

body:
## Summary
apps/stage is the surface that actually goes to air, and it is the only workspace package the lint gates never read: it is globally ignored, has no lint script, and CI never lints it. Remove the exemption, fix the hygiene findings, and hold the React-Compiler-class hook findings on a counted ratchet instead of a blanket off.

## Description
Add a stage block to eslint.config.js with the console's hygiene rules (no any, no `as unknown as`, no swallowed catch, JSON.parse only at a door, one keyboard file) and the react-hooks recommended set. Stage's doors are named, not waived: its two JSON decoders (clip.ts, voice/frame.ts) join the door list for the JSON.parse rule only, each a single function returning a typed result. Fold App.tsx's keydown listener into Controls.tsx, the stage's one declared keyboard file. Replace the 10 `as unknown as` casts (5 production, 5 test) with type guards or typed test doubles; route test-file JSON line reads through the stage decoders or a single test helper; fix OnAir.tsx:101's dependency list and the unused binding. The ~51 React-Compiler-class findings (react-hooks/refs, set-state-in-effect, preserve-manual-memoization, use-memo, immutability, purity), clustered in App.tsx's imperative playback refs, go into ESLint 10's native suppressions file via `--suppress-rule`: a per-file, per-rule counted set that fails on any new instance and only shrinks via --prune-suppressions. Add `lint` to apps/stage/package.json and a `stage lint` CI step (Card A's planner, if landed first, would demand exactly this step).

Techniques: ratchet-design and counted-set-snapshot (metric-gates - 'gating a metric that cannot be zeroed today'), excess-indicts-the-instrument (quality-gates - the refs cluster on one file is recorded as one baseline, not 46 independent defects), waiver-names-its-finding (door entries name files and the one rule they relax). Gate: architecture (lint topology). Coupled files outside the context: the stage sources listed in write_set (the gate cannot land red).

## Flow
- eslint.config.js: drop the `apps/stage/**` ignore; add the stage block; add the two stage decoders to the JSON.parse door; stage keyboard-file override
- fix ~25 hygiene findings in stage source and tests
- `eslint --suppress-rule` for the compiler-class hook rules only -> apps/stage/eslint-suppressions.json
- apps/stage/package.json `lint`; ci.yml `stage lint` step

## Expected impact
The on-air canvas gets the same untrusted-input discipline as the console; a new unchecked cast, raw listener or stray JSON parse in the broadcast path becomes a red build; the App.tsx refs debt becomes a visible, shrinking number instead of an unread exemption.

## Evaluation
Claim: stage source is lint-gated, hygiene at zero, compiler-class hook findings ratcheted.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no lint script; ignore present; every seed goes undetected)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - seeded violations written first and watched red
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: eslint.config.js:69 `"apps/stage/**",` inside ignores; eslint.config.js:73 `files: ["apps/console/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "packages/*/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]`. Probe output: `69 files 81 msgs`; [('react-hooks/refs', 46), ('no-restricted-syntax', 20), ('no-restricted-properties', 6), ('react-hooks/set-state-in-effect', 2), ('react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization', 2), ('react-hooks/use-memo', 1), ('react-hooks/immutability', 1), ('react-hooks/purity', 1), ('react-hooks/exhaustive-deps', 1), ('@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars', 1)]; per file: App.tsx 42, voice/useVoice.ts 8, fixture.test.ts 4, ClipStage.tsx 3. `npx eslint --help` lists --suppress-rule and --prune-suppressions (ESLint 10.13.0).

critic.reason: Grounded tightening of the broadcast package, but the declared write set cannot produce a green lint.

revision: Add apps/stage/src/fixture.test.ts, apps/stage/src/live.test.ts and apps/stage/src/voice/report.test.ts to write_set (they contain JSON.parse the stage block will flag, so case 1 cannot reach exit 0 without editing them).
